description.narrative:
Kisumu port is one of the critical assets that facilitates multimodal cargo transport from rail, road and water. It handles both containerized and conventional Cargo as well as pedestrians. Kisumu Port has a capacity to handle 50,000 TEUs or an equivalent of 200,000 metric tonnes. In KPA’s strategic plan for 2018-2022, KPA plans to increase Kisumu Port Capacity to 600,000 TEUs.
The Government of Kenya invested USD 7 million to rehabilitate Kisumu Port in 2019-2020 to boost intermodal transport through Lake Victoria and East Africa Region. The aim of the project was to revive maritime activities at Lake Victoria, create employment, spur economic growth, enhance connectivity, reduce pollution and facilitate regional trade through lake transport trade. It will connect Kisumu, Mwanza, Bukoba and Port bell through lake transport. The work undertaken by GOK included project design work and Environmental and Social Impact study (ESIA), concreting of the port yard, construction of the quayside (area along the water bank) including feeder jetties and piers, repairs of the linkspan (drawbridge used in moving vehicles on and off a vessel), repair of the dry dock and road works, building’s rehabilitation and provision of operations equipment including forklift trucks, mobile cranes and tractor-trailers for cargo handling. The expected results include reviving maritime activities at Lake Victoria, spur economic growth, create employment, enhance connectivity, reduce air pollution and facilitate regional trade through lake transport trade."
Further, Use of lake transport at Kisumu Port has been limited. Kenya shares lake borders with Tanzania and Uganda. Historically, marine transport on the lake, together with the rail network, formed an important component of an intermodal supply chain along the Central and Northern Corridor linking to Mombasa and Dar es Salaam seaports. Regular sailings used to take place between Port Bell and Kisumu (Kenya) on the Northern Corridor, Jinja and Port Bell (Uganda) and Mwanza (Tanzania) on the Central Corridor as well as between Mwanza and Kisumu. With an estimated population of 35 million living around the lake and its islands enhancing lake transport not only increases the market for Kenyan exports but also offers an opportunity to reduce the cost of cargo transport and reduce greenhouse gas
